devKeyboard.enable: Use the computer keyboard as a piano

mic.heading: Microphone
mic.intro: Place the microphone near the piano. It hears one note at a time; chords come later.
mic.unsupported: This browser can’t use the microphone. Use Chrome or Edge.
mic.denied: Microphone access was blocked. Allow it for this site in the browser’s site settings, then try again.
mic.error: The microphone couldn’t start. Check that it’s connected and not used by another app.
mic.thresholdHint: Lower it if soft notes are missed; raise it if noise is detected as notes.
mic.summary: Background noise: {noise} dB · Delay correction: {delay} ms
mic.headphones: To measure the delay, play any key on each click. Headphones help, so the microphone doesn’t hear the clicks.
mic.delayRunning: Play a key on each click: {beat} of {total}
mic.delayDone: Delay correction set to {ms} ms ({taps} of {total} clicks heard).
mic.failed: That didn’t work: not enough was heard. Try again, playing a little louder.

micCheck.heading: Microphone check
micCheck.intro: With both the MIDI cable and the microphone on, play notes across the keyboard. MIDI says which keys you really played, so this shows how well the microphone hears them.
micCheck.record: Record the audio, to help improve note detection
micCheck.saveHint: Saves one file (.json) with the microphone audio and the notes you played on MIDI. Put it in the project’s fixtures/mic folder.

sound.heading: Sound and timing

metronomeHints.auto: On when playing along, and when a lesson asks for it.
metronomeHints.on: Every exercise starts with the metronome on, waiting for each note too.
metronomeHints.off: Every exercise starts with the metronome off.

sound.intro: Bluetooth headphones and speakers play sound late (often 150–250 ms), and the browser can’t tell: the clicks come after the beat, and notes played with them look late. Measure the timing to make up for it: tap any key on your piano exactly with each click. It’s kept for each sound output, and followed when you switch.
sound.notMeasured: Not measured for this output yet.
sound.running: Tap a key exactly with each click: {beat} of {total}
sound.done: Clicks now play {ms} ms earlier ({taps} of {total} taps used).
sound.failed: Not enough taps were heard. Try again, tapping a key on every click.
sound.micFirst: Do this before measuring the microphone delay.

voice.heading: Your vocal range
voice.intro: Sing from your lowest comfortable note to your highest. It takes about a minute, with the microphone; the app stays quiet, so no headphones are needed.

help.comfortable: Sing an easy “ah”, at a pitch you could hold all day, and keep it for a moment.
help.lowest: Slide down slowly, as low as feels easy, then hold the lowest note for a moment.
help.highest: Now slide up slowly, as high as feels easy, and hold the highest note for a moment.

voice.dontPush: Don’t push: a note counts once it’s steady for about half a second.
voice.span: {semitones, plural, one {# semitone} other {# semitones}}, about {octaves} octaves
voice.voiceTypeNote: (only a guide: voice types are about more than range)
voice.micDenied: The microphone isn’t allowed. Allow it in the browser, then try again.
voice.micUnavailable: The range test needs a microphone, and none could be started.

data.confirmText: Your progress, settings and songs here are replaced with the ones in the file. Export them first if you want to keep them.

problems.notBackup: This file isn’t a Piano Teacher export.
problems.failed: The file couldn’t be imported. Nothing was changed.
